title: 6 free Android games I always install on every new phone
title_bn: 6 free Android games I always install on every new phone
author: TechPulse
excerpt: These games include engaging features without intrusive monetization and ads.
paragraph1: Megan Ellis / Android AuthorityI love games, whether they’re on mobile or PC. Android games in particular keep me busy during flights or while standing in long queues. As a result, I’ve amassed a collection of favorites over the years that I always install on every new phone I getThere are premium games that deserve your money, but when you have a limited budget, free games come in handy to pass the time. I always make sure to keep these gems in my arsenal so that I have an alternative to doomscrolling social media.What is the most important aspect of a free Android game for you?4 votes1. Pokémon GoMegan Ellis / Android AuthorityWhile you might assume that Pokémon Go isn’t active anymore, it still has a vibrant community going 10 years after its launch. I started playing again in 2025, and although I initially found it a literal pain to play, joining a local community greatly helped with the social aspects.The game has also undergone some quality-of-life improvements that make it easier to hatch eggs, trade, and level up friendships with other players. In addition to this, frequent events mean that there’s always something to do or work towards. In fact, Go Fest Global 2026 just took place, with it being the first free edition of the event. The game is completely free to join and play, although there are premium items and passes available. However, if you play your cards right, you can get a healthy amount of in-game currency without spending anything. Many Android games may keep you distracted for an hour or so, but Pokémon Go is an immersive game that keeps you playing and strategizing significantly longer. 2. OneUpPuzzleLite When I describe OneUp, I call it “Sudoku, but harder.” The puzzle game is challenging, but also incredibly rewarding.
paragraph2: Rather than using animations and gamification to keep you engaged, the accomplishment you feel when completing puzzles provides the rush you need.The app is incredibly lightweight, featuring just the puzzles and rules. Like Sudoku, you need to fill out numbers in their horizontal and vertical rows. However, walls divide these rows into smaller segments that also need to be filled out. The game also includes a timer so you can see how long it takes you to solve a puzzle.I describe OneUp as Sudoku, but harder. It's a must for logic puzzle fans.I first got started with these puzzles on the OneUp website but wanted to get in more practice. I found the dedicated mobile app and sunk hours into solving its puzzles. I enjoyed the experience so much that I even ended up buying the premium version of the game, which includes even more puzzles. 3. Dingbats – Between the lines Dingbats is a game where you use visual word arrangements to guess the phrase it depicts. These are common sayings depicted through visual wordplay. For example, dividing the word “promise” in two illustrates the phrase “broken promise”.The available letters and slots you need to fill in also give you a clue about the possible phrases depicted in the puzzle. If you get stuck, you can spend coins to reveal a letter to help you out.Dingbats is the perfect game for people who love language and puns.
paragraph3: While the game may be a bit minimalistic for some, it’s still an engaging time-killer. You need to finish a certain number of puzzles to proceed to the next level, but you don’t have to deal with limited lives or other time-gating. 4. Little Alchemy 2 There is something about the matching and categorizing of Little Alchemy 2 that scratches an itch in my brain that I didn’t know was there. The aim of the game is to mix different objects together to discover more ingredients, and then use those new items to create more.You start off with a very limited set of items, but your catalog grows with your discoveries. For example, mixing earth and water creates mud. Eventually, your screen is teeming with items and possibilities, making more creative combinations available. My personal favorite is when you unlock the human and animal categories and combine them to create different final items.There are also countless paths to arrive at the game’s items. On my latest playthrough, I was able to unlock the atomic bomb before I managed to unlock the concept of life.Little Alchemy 2 keeps you busy for hours as you mix and match ingredients to unlock new items.The experience is simple yet satisfying, and with over 700 items to unlock in the game, it can also keep you busy for hours. 5. Two Dots Two Dots is probably one of the first puzzle games that held my attention for a very long time. I think of it as a minimalist take on match games. However, rather than swiveling candy, you need to link up dots vertically and horizontally.
paragraph4: As you progress, the mechanics become more complex, introducing different types of dots and obstacles. With so many boosts available, as you become more skilled at the game, you’ll likely collect enough resources so that you no longer need to watch ads for these boosts. I occasionally watch an ad for an extra life, but there are plenty of in-game bonuses that give you unlimited lives for a short period.While it has leaned more into ads over time, Two Dots still provides a great free experience.The game has its main path, as well as limited-time events and challenges to keep you busy. The main path is also updated frequently enough to keep you engaged. It has introduced a game pass. However, I focus on the free benefits. I’ve reached level 4,170 without ever spending a cent on the game.The downside is that the game has become more monetized over time, meaning that its once optional ads have become more prominent. I used to only encounter these ads if I wanted to gain an in-game item or extra life. However, now ads appear as banners during the game. You also receive full-screen ads occasionally after completing levels. On the bright side, they’re still a lot less frequent than many other mobile games. 6. PlaySimple Cryptogram Cryptograms are my new favorite type of puzzle games, but finding an app that balances difficulty without overloading you with ads took some time. Eventually, I settled on PlaySimple Cryptogram.
paragraph5: Cryptograms essentially require you to decode phrases using a cipher. A few letters are provided, along with their corresponding numbers. You then use these numbers to fill in additional instances of the letters. Eventually, it becomes easier to figure out which words are included in the phrase.PlaySimple's Crytogram game lets you feel like a code breaker without being interrupted by intrusive ads.What I like about PlaySimple’s cryptogram app is that it doesn’t autofill all instances of a letter once decoded. I found that apps that did this made the puzzle too easy. It also supports a dark mode, and its ads aren’t intrusive. There is a point in a puzzle where you start figuring out the phrase quickly, but the path to get there is challenging and rewarding. Wading through the Play Store to find decent Android games can be a time-consuming undertaking. And even when you find good games, they may become worse over time due to monetization strategies. However, these free games always make it into my rotation because of the way they balance features and monetization.FollowThank you for being part of our community. title: Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay Gaming Headset Review
title_bn: Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay Gaming Headset Review
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay offers solid sound, quality comms, and never-ending uptime at a reduced price. There’s a handful of trade-offs, but this headset has more wins than losses and is definitely worth considering.
paragraph1: The Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay offers solid sound, quality comms, and never-ending uptime at a reduced price. There’s a handful of trade-offs, but this headset has more wins than losses and is definitely worth considering. Pros +Balanced sound profile, customizable with Glorious Core software +Dual-mode connectivity: 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth +Remains connected when swapping batteries +No more battery life anxiety Cons -No simultaneous 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth -A bit plasticky, floppy earcups Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test. These days, the best gaming headsets tend to share a lot of qualities. They all sound great, have decent microphones, and are comfortable enough for full day gaming sessions. And, once you pass a certain price point, almost all of them are wireless. For years, that meant keeping track of battery statuses and remembering to charge or be faced with plugging in or logging out to recharge.The Glorious GHS Wireless InfinitePlay changes all that with its hot-swappable battery system. Unlike other headsets with hot-swappable batteries, like the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless and the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II, the Wireless InfinitePlay also has a built-in battery to keep the sound pumping and comms connected while swapping batteries. It sounds great and is plenty comfortable, but does it earn its $230 asking price? I think it does — and, compared to its competition, it almost feels like a bargain.
paragraph2: Swipe to scroll horizontally Driver Type 40mm angled dynamic drivers Frequency Response 20 Hz - 20 kHz Design Style Over-ear, closed back Microphone Type Omni-directional, detachable Connectivity Bluetooth 5.3, 2.4GHz, USB Type-C Weight 12.8 oz / 361 g (with mic and battery), 11.3 oz / 319 g (headset only) Cord Length 6.5 ft Battery Life Up to 85 hours per battery (x2), three hour internal backup for battery swaps Lighting None Software Glorious Core MSRP/Price at Time of Review $229.99 (Glorious) Release Date July 21, 2026 Design and Comfort of the Glorious GHS Wireless InfinitePlayThe Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay is the epitome of stealth. There's no RGB and the only-colored accent is at the edges of its elastic headband. It's only when you look closely that you'll see the Glorious logo in subtle gray on the right ear cup or the headband accents or the flashes of the brand’s iconic orange inside each ear cup.Apart from those subtle accents, the headset's blacked out appearance makes it a good fit for use on the go. I wouldn’t give a second thought to wearing these out of the house if the need arose. And you may want to, because even though its asking price ($230) is lower than some of the competition, these are still pricey enough that you may want to wear them for more than just gaming — and they live up to that. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Glorious has put a lot of effort into ensuring that the Wireless InfinitePlay is exceptionally comfortable. The headset uses an elastic headstrap that runs beneath its plastic headband.
paragraph3: Using plastic allows for a relatively lightweight design, and the elastic helps distribute what weight there is. In the two weeks I had the headset in for testing, I didn’t experience any head pain, which is something I’m particularly susceptible to.The ear cushions are made of a soft, pliable foam that’s accommodating to glasses while still offering a good seal around each ear. They’re trimmed in fabric and are very breathable, but be warned: plenty of sound makes its way in and out of these headphones, so don’t listen to anything at high volume you wouldn’t want your roommate to hear. There’s also no ANC, which could be a deal-breaker when other flagship headsets include it. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The grip force is strong enough to create a seal, but the headset has a bad case of floppy earcups that work against that. Each earcup rotates to lay flat around your neck — usually a plus — but the yokes (hinges) holding them just aren’t strong enough to keep them from turning on their own. This doesn’t make a big difference for normal listening, but between the floppy cups, reliance on plastic, and the light weight, this doesn't feel like a $230 headset when you’re picking it up and putting it down.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.The headset sports dual-mode connectivity with support for 2.4 GHz wireless and Bluetooth 5.X and can swap between them on the fly with a press behind the right earcup. Changing sources is fast and reliable, but I still wish they were simultaneous and could play at the same time.The headset’s hallmark feature, however, is its hot-swappable battery system.
paragraph4: Like the Turtle Beach Stealth Pro II and the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless, the InfinitePlay comes with two batteries and a base station that connects to your source and recharges your second battery. When it’s time to switch, you simply eject the battery from its spring-loaded slot on the bottom of the right cup and slide the new one into place. If you don’t need the battery system, or don’t want the base station connected to your PC all the time, you can unplug a USB Type-C dongle from the back of the dock and use it standalone for a lower profile experience. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Where the Glorious Wireless InfinitePlay truly becomes unique, however, is that it supplements its two removable batteries with a three-hour built-in back-up that can’t be removed. While every other headset as of this writing (correct me in the comments if I’m missing anything) disconnects briefly when changing batteries, the second you remove swappable battery from the earcup, the standby kicks in so you never lose connection. It’s surprisingly high capacity, too, lasting around three hours before finally requiring you to put the second battery in.This is a genuinely useful feature and one that I expect will become standard among the “swappable battery” headsets. It’s just so convenient in comparison and truly makes this headset feel “infinite” in a way its competitors don’t. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)That isn’t to say the Wireless InfinitePlay should instantly be your go-to pick in this category. Its knobs are functional when worn and annoying when not. Each ear cup features a tall knob. The left controls Game/Chat balance and the right controls volume. Neither is labeled, so there’s a good chance you’ll accidentally turn the wrong knob and then wonder why your volume is so low (because the knob is tilted more toward Chat). There’s also a microphone mute switch just below on the left and a power button on the right.
paragraph5: The problem is that in the pursuit of making these knobs easy to manipulate by making them tall, Glorious also made them super easy to hit by mistake when it’s hanging around your neck. Earcups up? You’ll hit them with your shoulder. Earcups down? You’ll need to watch your head and chin. Neither of these are deal breakers, but it’s a strange problem to have when it’s so apparent in actual use. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Audio Performance of the Glorious GHS Wireless InfinitePlay To drive with sonics, the InfinitePlay uses a pair of custom-tuned 40mm dynamic drivers. In the gaming headset space, this is a common configuration, but Glorious sets it apart in several ways. The first is that the drivers are angled within each ear cup. This is a technique found on many high-end audiophile headphones with the aim of increasing the realism and spatial details of what you’re listening to. The angle is intended to mimic how sounds enter your ear in real life: typically off-axis and guided by the Pinna. The impact is real but not profound, though it translates to some pretty great competitive acoustics when paired with Windows Sonic and Dolby Atmos.

title: The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro could get a hefty GPU upgrade to justify its high price
title_bn: The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro could get a hefty GPU upgrade to justify its high price
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro could slice and dice its predecessor in one category.
paragraph1: Nick Fernandez / Android AuthorityTL;DR A trusted leaker reports that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Gen 6 Pro will have a GPU with six slices. Qualcomm’s previous Elite chips have GPUs with three slices, while the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 GPU has just two slices. This leak therefore suggests that the new chips could bring major graphical gains. Qualcomm will hold its annual Snapdragon Summit next month, and it’s expected to unveil the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro. The Pro chip in particular is rumored to be very expensive, but a new leak suggests we could be in for a major gaming upgrade.
paragraph2: Leaker Digital Chat Station has claimed on Weibo that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series GPUs have six slices. This suggests a massive GPU upgrade for next-generation Snapdragon chips. Check out the machine-translated screenshot below.Every Snapdragon flagship processor since the Snapdragon 8 Elite uses a so-called sliced GPU architecture. This sees the GPU’s shader cores and other fixed-function hardware blocks divided into slices.
paragraph3: This approach allows the chipset to dynamically set the frequency for each GPU slice as needed, rather than running the entire GPU at a high clock speed. This should result in better performance, load-balancing, and power efficiency.The Snapdragon 8 Elite and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 have three GPU slices, while the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 has just two slices. So it stands to reason that the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series could see huge performance and efficiency gains with the switch to six slices.Double the slices doesn’t necessarily mean double the performance, as other factors like clock speed, cache, and more will also have a significant influence.
paragraph4: For example, Qualcomm could opt for more slices but a reduced clock speed. Nevertheless, it looks like mobile gamers should keep an eye on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro.Unfortunately, numerous leaks point to the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro seeing a big price hike over the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. So you might have to splash out a ton of cash if you want a phone with this processor.FollowThank you for being part of our community.

title: AI Concierge Startup Hulp Raises $2.6 Mn From Sparrow Capital, BITKRAFT
title_bn: AI Concierge Startup Hulp Raises $2.6 Mn From Sparrow Capital, BITKRAFT
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Household assistance startup Hulp has raised $2.6 Mn (about ₹25 Cr) in a seed funding round led by VC firms…
paragraph1: SUMMARYGurugram-based household assistance startup Hulp raised $2.6 Mn in a seed funding round led by Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures This comes at a time when India’s affluent class is expanding and several new-age companies are seeking to offer concierge services to cater to their aspirational lifestyles Hulp, which is currently only active in Delhi-NCR, plans to expand into Mumbai, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai over the next two years Household assistance startup Hulp has raised $2.6 Mn (about ₹25 Cr) in a seed funding round led by VC firms Sparrow Capital and BITKRAFT Ventures. While early stage VC DeVC also participated in the round, multiple angel investors including PB Fintech cofounder and chairman Yashish Dahiya, also participated in the round.
paragraph2: The Delhi NCR-based startup will deploy the fresh capital to scale its AI platform, hire senior leaders, and strengthen technology infrastructure to expand service coverage across metro cities. Founded in 2026 by ex-Policybazaar CBO Tarun Mathur, alongside ex-Mitgo India MD Neha Kulwal and Vishal Singh Khutel, Hulp operates a concierge service that combines AI automation with dedicated human assistants. Users can contact assistants through WhatsApp or its mobile app and delegate tasks through a voice note. The platform claims to handle daily tasks across more than 15 categories including kitchen management, runner services, administrative filings, travel and event bookings, and restaurant reservations.
paragraph3: It plans to expand operations into Mumbai, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad, and Chennai over the next two years. India’s affluent consumers are projected to cross the 10 Cr mark by 2027, according to a report by Goldman Sachs Research. New-age tech companies are increasingly aiming to cater to this market, driving the rise of the convenience economy. Quick commerce and instant home services are the most widely known examples of how this trend is playing out.
paragraph4: However, startups offering concierge services are also seeking to serve the needs of aspirational Indians. Notably, food delivery giant Swiggy operates in this segment, offering on-demand concierge services for wealthy customers via its Crew app. Former American Express executive Manoj Adlakha’s bootstrapped venture RedBeryl, founded in 2023, is another notable player whose services are invite-only and span a range of categories from fine dining to sports and entertainment. Last year, Indulge Global of Shark Tank fame also bagged $1 Mn funding to scale its own luxury concierge services platform.

title: Crazed modder turns NAS into a gaming PC with RTX 5060 hanging from the side, boosts frame rate by 828% — Frankenstein rig hides dedicated PSU in drive bay, breaks Time Spy world record for the onboard CPU
title_bn: Crazed modder turns NAS into a gaming PC with RTX 5060 hanging from the side, boosts frame rate by 828% — Frankenstein rig hides dedicated PSU in drive bay, breaks Time Spy world record for the onboard CPU
author: TechPulse
excerpt: A modder has attached a full-sized RTX 5060 graphics card to a ZimaCube 2 NAS server and achieved up to 8x faster performance in games. The jerry-rigged setup doesn't look the most polished, and the CPU is heavily bottlenecked, but it still, uh, exis
paragraph1: (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube) It seems the global component crisis has skyrocketed the prices of storage to the point where some alternative ways of utilizing a NAS have popped up. YouTube PC enthusiast TrashBench recently took a ZimaCube 2 NAS and modded it into a gaming PC, driven by an RTX 5060 graphics card. Despite the low-power laptop CPU inside the server, the results still showed an astronomical improvement in gaming performance across the board, improving frame rates by 828% in some tests and breaking the Time Spy world record for the Intel Core i5-1235U CPU. Can a Server Replace a Gaming PC? - YouTube Watch On For context, the ZimaCube 2 is powered by an Intel Core i5-1235U CPU, which is an Alder Lake chip featuring just two P-cores and eight E-cores, alongside Iris Xe integrated graphics. The iGPU is weak because that's all that's needed for a server (if it's needed at all). This system was never intended for gaming, but the motherboard inside has a vacant PCIe 4.
paragraph2: 0 x16 slot, making this NAS the perfect candidate to be liberated by some questionable mods.At first, the tests showed the iGPU hitting around 18 FPS in Hitman 3 on 1080p with low settings. Cyberpunk 2077 was even worse with just 13 FPS, while Shadow of the Tomb Raider was the most promising title, achieving 31 FPS. Putting an AMD Radeon Pro WX5100 workstation GPU (a cut-down version of the RX 480) in the board's slot helped raise the numbers a bit, around 40% on average, but the updated performance was still not enough to be classified as playable.TrashBench proceeded to connect an RTX 5060 to the x16 slot with a riser cable and just let it hang outside the case, since the card was way too big to fit inside. Of course, this wasn't ideal and would restrict airflow quite a bit, so he devised a 3D-printed frame that would hold the GPU in place, while zip-tying the other end to the case directly. The final result might not exactly look polished, but it was firm enough to conduct benchmarks.
paragraph3: (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)Keep in mind that all this jury-rigging was possible due to the ZimaCube's unique design. The chassis has large cutouts across its chassis, allowing the riser cable to easily protrude from the left. To power the RTX 5060, TrashBench removed all the hard drive caddies so that the system's drive bay was left completely empty. He then fit a 750W SFX power supply inside with an extension cable that ran up to the GPU's power connector. The front cover of this NAS is magnetic, so everything was nicely hidden behind it. (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube) (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)TrashBench's retesting showed Hitman 3 running at 167 FPS on average, which is an 827% improvement over the stock 18 FPS, or more than nine times faster. Similarly, Cyberpunk 2077 got a 7x boost, going from 13 FPS to 90 FPS.
paragraph4: Framerates in Shadow of the Tomb Raider "only" quadrupled, as the RTX 5060 achieved an average of 124 FPS compared to 31 FPS with the iGPU.TrashBench didn't stop there and, true to his nature, wanted to freeze the CPU to try and see if he could get even better results. The issue was that the chip never throttled to begin with, and the GPU was already bottlenecked, so running an antifreeze loop actually worsened performance. The silicon designed to run a storage server had achieved its maximum potential.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)Unfortunately, this variant of the ZimaCube 2 does cost $1,299 to start with so you're much better off just building a regular PC even today. It also doesn't come with Windows, and the BIOS was never configured to run a dedicated GPU, so you have to always have something plugged into the iGPU's display output for the dGPU to display anything.
paragraph5: Still, as a wild experiment, we can call this one a success. When he’s not working, you’ll find him bending tubes for his ever-evolving custom water-loop gaming rig or benchmarking the latest CPUs and GPUs just for fun.

The iGPU is weak because that's all that's needed for a server (if it's needed at all). This system was never intended for gaming, but the motherboard inside has a vacant PCIe 4.
bangla_paragraph2: 0 x16 slot, making this NAS the perfect candidate to be liberated by some questionable mods.At first, the tests showed the iGPU hitting around 18 FPS in Hitman 3 on 1080p with low settings. Cyberpunk 2077 was even worse with just 13 FPS, while Shadow of the Tomb Raider was the most promising title, achieving 31 FPS. Putting an AMD Radeon Pro WX5100 workstation GPU (a cut-down version of the RX 480) in the board's slot helped raise the numbers a bit, around 40% on average, but the updated performance was still not enough to be classified as playable.TrashBench proceeded to connect an RTX 5060 to the x16 slot with a riser cable and just let it hang outside the case, since the card was way too big to fit inside. Of course, this wasn't ideal and would restrict airflow quite a bit, so he devised a 3D-printed frame that would hold the GPU in place, while zip-tying the other end to the case directly. The final result might not exactly look polished, but it was firm enough to conduct benchmarks.
bangla_paragraph3: (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)Keep in mind that all this jury-rigging was possible due to the ZimaCube's unique design. The chassis has large cutouts across its chassis, allowing the riser cable to easily protrude from the left. To power the RTX 5060, TrashBench removed all the hard drive caddies so that the system's drive bay was left completely empty. He then fit a 750W SFX power supply inside with an extension cable that ran up to the GPU's power connector. The front cover of this NAS is magnetic, so everything was nicely hidden behind it. (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube) (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)TrashBench's retesting showed Hitman 3 running at 167 FPS on average, which is an 827% improvement over the stock 18 FPS, or more than nine times faster. Similarly, Cyberpunk 2077 got a 7x boost, going from 13 FPS to 90 FPS.
bangla_paragraph4: Framerates in Shadow of the Tomb Raider "only" quadrupled, as the RTX 5060 achieved an average of 124 FPS compared to 31 FPS with the iGPU.TrashBench didn't stop there and, true to his nature, wanted to freeze the CPU to try and see if he could get even better results. The issue was that the chip never throttled to begin with, and the GPU was already bottlenecked, so running an antifreeze loop actually worsened performance. The silicon designed to run a storage server had achieved its maximum potential.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox. (Image credit: TrashBench on YouTube)Unfortunately, this variant of the ZimaCube 2 does cost $1,299 to start with so you're much better off just building a regular PC even today. It also doesn't come with Windows, and the BIOS was never configured to run a dedicated GPU, so you have to always have something plugged into the iGPU's display output for the dGPU to display anything.
bangla_paragraph5: Still, as a wild experiment, we can call this one a success. title: Sarvam To Raise $74 Mn In Series B Extension From NVIDIA, Others
title_bn: Sarvam To Raise $74 Mn In Series B Extension From NVIDIA, Others
author: TechPulse
excerpt: AI unicorn Sarvam is set to raise another $74 Mn (about ₹697.8 Cr) in an extension of its ongoing Series…
paragraph1: SUMMARYSarvam is raising an additional $74 Mn in an extension of its ongoing $300 Mn Series B round, with backing from NVIDIA, Glade Brook, Gaja Capital, and Indigo Ventures The funding strengthens Sarvam's war chest as it accelerates its ambitions to build a full-stack sovereign AI ecosystem, expand globally, and compete with leading international AI players This comes amid Sarvam's rapid product expansion, including the launch of its AI coding agent, India-hosted inference platform, upcoming trillion-parameter model, and broader push into enterprise AI infrastructure and developer tools AI unicorn Sarvam is set to raise another $74 Mn (about ₹697.8 Cr) in an extension of its ongoing Series B funding round from a clutch of investors, including NVIDIA, Glade Brook, Gaja Capital, Indigo Ventures, among others. According to MCA filings accessed by Inc42, the Bengaluru-based startup’s approved a resolution during an extraordinary general meeting held on July 24 to raise ₹697.8 Cr from around 13 investors. Of the total amount, NVIDIA will invest ₹237.9 Cr in Sarvam, followed by growth equity firm Glade Brook, which will invest ₹190.
paragraph2: 3 Cr. Among domestic investors, Gaja Capital will invest ₹95.1 Cr, while Indigo Ventures will pump in committed ₹30 Cr. The remaining capital will come from HNIs and family offices. Recently launched AI-focused VC fund Activate also participated in the latest round, according to founder Aakrit Vaish. In a LinkedIn post, he noted that this is the “single largest capital commitment we’ve ever made to a company, bringing together a number of our strategic LPs and family offices in support of Sovereign AI in India”.
paragraph3: However, he didn’t disclose Activate’s exact contribution to Sarvam. The proposed fundraise is part of Sarvam’s ongoing $300 Mn Series B round at a valuation of $1.5 Bn. In June, the startup announced the first tranche of the round worth up to $234 Mn (about ₹2,210 Cr), led by HCL Tech. It also saw participation from Bessemer Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners. At the time, Sarvam said it would use the capital to strengthen its research into next-generation AI models, expand its compute infrastructure and scale deployments across sectors.
paragraph4: The development comes a week after Sarvam hosted its inaugural developer conference, Sarvam Epoch, unveiling its ambitions of becoming a full-stack AI venture, expanding its ambit to infrastructure, document intelligence applications, and enterprise tools like a coding copilot and AI agents. The AI unicorn unveiled a new AI coding agent for engineering teams — Sarvam Code, which breaks down the coding workflow into three separate models, including a planner, a worker and a verifier, to reliably determine when a coding task is complete. Sarvam Code will take on foreign competitors like Claude and Codex. Sarvam also announced plans to roll out a trillion-parameter AI model within six months, targeting use cases spanning coding, cybersecurity, simulation, science, and more. As part of its global expansion strategy, the startup announced a new office in San Francisco and appointed Devendra Singh Chaplot, formerly part of the founding teams at Mistral AI and Thinking Machines Lab, as an advisor. Perhaps its biggest announcement was Sarvam Inference, an inference platform that serves frontier open-source AI models using infrastructure hosted within India.
paragraph5: The platform currently supports Sarvam’s own 105 Bn parameter model alongside open models such as GLM 5.2 and Gemma 4. Positioned as part of the startup’s push for “token sovereignty”, the platform is aimed at developers, enterprises and government organisations seeking access to frontier AI models while ensuring inference workloads remain within India to meet data residency requirements. Additionally, the unicorn opened up its voice-agent platform Samvaad, which was earlier only available to select enterprise customers. Inc42 previously reported that Sarvam would open up Samvaad through a self-serve model targeting startups, SMBs, developers and individual users. title: It’s 2026, and I still can’t trust Google’s Pixel phones
title_bn: It’s 2026, and I still can’t trust Google’s Pixel phones
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Fool me once, Google...
paragraph1: Shimul Sood / Android AuthorityI’ve been using Pixels for as long as I can remember, which is why admitting this feels a little strange: I don’t fully trust Pixels in 2026. That isn’t because Google makes bad phones. In many ways, the Pixel experience has never been better. The software is polished, Gemini takes the hassle out of everyday tasks, and features like Magic Eraser, Best Take, and Call Notes have become so ingrained in my routine that I instantly miss them whenever I pick up another phone. However, Pixels also leave a few crucial boxes unchecked.Every time I consider making a Pixel my only phone, something holds me back. It has little to do with Google’s AI ambitions or its clean take on Android. The problem is far more basic than that. In 2026, I need my primary smartphone to be dependable in a few areas I cannot compromise on, and despite all the progress Google has made, Pixels still have not earned that level of trust from me.Would you trust a Pixel as your only phone in 2026?43 votesThe heat never takes a day offC. Scott Brown / Android AuthorityFor me, it all starts with performance. Or, more specifically, how Pixel phones behave when I actually use them throughout the day. Until very recently, the Pixel 10 Pro was my daily driver, and it tested my patience more than I’d like to admit. We’ve all heard the conversations around Tensor chips not being the fastest or most efficient, but this goes beyond benchmark scores. It’s something I’ve experienced firsthand across multiple generations, including the Pixel 8, Pixel 9, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10 Pro, and now the Pixel 10a.
paragraph2: The top half of the phone starts heating up until it becomes genuinely uncomfortable to hold.They get hot. Really hot. And I’m not talking about the occasional spike while installing an update or gaming for an hour. I’m talking about regular, everyday tasks. Open a handful of apps, spend a little too long taking photos and selfies, record a few high-resolution videos, or multitask for a while, and I can almost predict what’s about to happen. The top half of the phone starts heating up until it becomes genuinely uncomfortable to hold.For the longest time, I blamed the weather, my own usage, or yet another software bug that I hoped the next update would fix. I wanted to believe there was a reasonable explanation because, honestly, I wanted to keep loving my Pixel. So I tried everything — I used it outdoors, indoors, in air-conditioned rooms, and during relatively light use. The result barely changed. That same uncomfortable warmth kept showing up, regardless of where I was or what I was doing.Living life one percent at a timeJoe Maring / Android AuthorityIf performance is my biggest complaint, battery life comes in at a very close second. I’ll be the first to admit that I’m terrible at remembering to charge my phone. More often than not, I’m plugging it in just a few minutes before leaving the house, and that’s completely on me. But even on the days when I do everything right — charge it to 100% before stepping out, I still don’t have complete faith that my Pixel will comfortably last until I get back home.
paragraph3: That’s the bigger issue.My daily routine isn’t particularly demanding. I’m usually listening to music during my commute, replying to messages, scrolling through social media now and then, taking a few photos, and spending a good portion of the day on work calls. It’s a fairly typical workload, and one I’d expect any modern flagship to handle.I hate having to manage my phone around its battery instead of simply using it.Instead, I find myself constantly glancing at the battery percentage, mentally calculating how much longer it’ll last, and whether it’s time to switch on Battery Saver. I hate having to manage my phone around its battery instead of simply using it.Stephen Radochia / Android AuthorityI’ve also gone down the rabbit hole of every battery-saving trick I could find. Adaptive Battery, Battery Saver, restricting background activity, turning off features I barely use — you name it, I’ve tried it. None of those changes made a meaningful difference to how much I trusted the phone by the end of the day.To make matters worse, the Pixel's idle battery drain only adds to that frustration.To make matters worse, the Pixel’s idle battery drain only adds to that frustration. There have been plenty of times when I’ve left the phone untouched for hours, only to pick it up and find that it has mysteriously lost a noticeable chunk of battery. Google has said it fixed the issue for most users, but that hasn’t been my experience. Judging by the number of reports from owners of the Pixel 9 series and Pixel 10 lineup, I’m clearly not the only one still dealing with it.At this point, I’ve stopped assuming my Pixel will get me through the day.
paragraph4: Instead, I leave home with a second phone whenever I can, because the moment your primary phone needs a backup, it’s hard to call it a phone you truly trust.The world’s longest charging breakJoe Maring / Android AuthorityAnd don’t even get me started on the charging speeds, because that’s where my patience completely runs out.Out of pure curiosity and maybe a little spite, I decided to see how slow my Pixel 10 Pro really was. One morning before work, I plugged it in at around 3% and went about my usual routine. I stretched for a bit, took a long shower, made myself breakfast, ate it, cleaned the kitchen, packed my bag, and got everything ready before leaving for work. By the time I came back, I’d spent roughly an hour and 15 minutes away from the charger. Surely the phone would be at 100%, right? No, it was still sitting at 68%.I had finished an entire morning routine before my phone had even finished charging.I couldn’t help but laugh when I saw the battery percentage. I had finished an entire morning routine before my phone had even finished charging. At that point, it almost felt like the Pixel was politely asking me to slow down and enjoy life while it figured things out.As if the slow charging wasn’t frustrating enough, it usually comes with an unwanted bonus: heat. The moment the phone is plugged in, it starts getting noticeably warm, sometimes to the point where it’s uncomfortable to pick up. So not only does it take ages to charge, but it also turns into a tiny hand warmer while doing it. That’s not exactly the kind of multitasking I was hoping for.
paragraph5: I’m still waiting for a better signalJoe Maring / Android AuthorityAnd just when I think I’ve run out of reasons to complain, my Pixel reminds me that the network experience deserves its own section. For some reason, my Pixel 10 Pro has developed a rather unique talent: pretending incoming calls don’t exist.My Pixel 10 Pro has developed a rather unique talent: pretending incoming calls don't exist.Sometimes the phone rings, sometimes it doesn’t, and on the rare occasion it actually decides to cooperate, the call quality can still be an adventure. I’ve had moments where I had to leave my desk, walk over to my Wi-Fi router, and continue the conversation from there, as if better reception was hiding behind it. It’s funny the first time. By the tenth time, not so much.Joe Maring / Android AuthorityThe most frustrating part is that you never know when it’s going to happen. Over the past month, I’ve realized my phone has silently ignored several incoming calls without giving me so much as a missed call notification. At first, I assumed my device was having a bad day. Then I looked online and realized I wasn’t alone. Plenty of Pixel users on Reddit have reported the same problem, and we even covered those complaints ourselves.I can’t keep beta testing my patienceJoe Maring / Android AuthorityHonestly, I could keep going. There are plenty of frustrations I’ve run into over the years, but you probably get the idea by now.What disappoints me the most isn’t that these issues exist — it’s that many of them have followed me across multiple generations of Pixel phones.

title: OpenAI, Anthropic AI agents targeted real people and organisations during cyber tests
title_bn: OpenAI, Anthropic AI agents targeted real people and organisations during cyber tests
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The UK's AI Security Institute found that AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI performed unsanctioned actions during security tests
paragraph1: The UK's AI Security Institute found that AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI performed unsanctioned actions during security testsOpenAI CEO Sam Altman.(REUTERS)Britain's AI Security Institute has said that it found AI agents from Anthropic and OpenAI engaging in "unsanctioned" actions against real people and organisations during security evaluations conducted to assess the AI models' abilities.“On 28th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations,” AISI wrote in a blog post.AISI says that the incident occurred when the AI agents were given a cybersecurity challenge. The agency says that it ran the challenge 122 times across seven frontier AI models. It says that AI agents took ‘autonomous unsanctioned action’ on the internet in 10 of those scenarios, targeting real people and organisations.However, AISI catalogued around 19 scenarios where the AI agents took unauthorized actions.
paragraph2: It says almost all of the behaviours came from Anthropic's Mythos 5 model, while two actions were attributed to OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol with safety classifiers disabled.“In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering, creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code,” AISI wrote.OpenAI responds:OpenAI clarified the behaviour of its model in a separate blog post, where it said that the recent incidents were separate from the Hugging Face breach. The company says that with AI model capabilities rapidly advancing, the security and safety systems around them also need to evolve.“The incidents underscore the importance of collaborating across the industry and with third-party evaluators to evolve the standards for testing environments and practices as models become more capable,” OpenAI wrote.
paragraph3: OpenAI also revealed a separate incident involving cybersecurity firm Irregular. During an evaluation, the AI models were told to find hidden information and exploit weaknesses within a simulated environment and were told they did not have access to the internet.However, a ‘misconfiguration’ in the testing environment allowed the models to access the internet.Subsequently, OpenAI revealed that GPT-5.6 Sol exploited a real website by taking advantage of a ‘basic security vulnerability’. However, OpenAI says that its model believed the website was part of the simulated environment, and that this scenario did not involve breaching a sandbox via a zero-day vulnerability like the Hugging Face incident.Meanwhile, Anthropic, while responding to the controversy in a statement quoted by Reuters, said, "We're grateful to the UK AISI for their leadership on this incident, which underscores the need for a broader conversation about how to safely evaluate increasingly capable AI agents."About the AuthorAman GuptaAman Gupta is a Digital Content Producer at LiveMint with over 3.
paragraph4:
5 years of experience covering the technology landscape. He specializes in artificial intelligence and consumer technology, reporting on everything from the ethical debates around AI models to shifts in the smartphone market.
His reporting is grounded in first-hand testing, independent analysis, and a focus on how technology impacts everyday users. He holds a PG Diploma in Radio and Television Journalism from the Indian Institute of Mass Communication, Delhi (Class of 2022).
Outside the newsroom, he spends his time reading biographies, hunting for the perfect coffee beans, or planning his next trip.

In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering, creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code,” AISI wrote.OpenAI responds:OpenAI clarified the behaviour of its model in a separate blog post, where it said that the recent incidents were separate from the Hugging Face breach. The company says that with AI model capabilities rapidly advancing, the security and safety systems around them also need to evolve.“The incidents underscore the importance of collaborating across the industry and with third-party evaluators to evolve the standards for testing environments and practices as models become more capable,” OpenAI wrote.
bangla_paragraph3: OpenAI also revealed a separate incident involving cybersecurity firm Irregular. During an evaluation, the AI models were told to find hidden information and exploit weaknesses within a simulated environment and were told they did not have access to the internet.However, a ‘misconfiguration’ in the testing environment allowed the models to access the internet.Subsequently, OpenAI revealed that GPT-5.6 Sol exploited a real website by taking advantage of a ‘basic security vulnerability’. However, OpenAI says that its model believed the website was part of the simulated environment, and that this scenario did not involve breaching a sandbox via a zero-day vulnerability like the Hugging Face incident.Meanwhile, Anthropic, while responding to the controversy in a statement quoted by Reuters, said, "We're grateful to the UK AISI for their leadership on this incident, which underscores the need for a broader conversation about how to safely evaluate increasingly capable AI agents."About the AuthorAman GuptaAman Gupta is a Digital Content Producer at LiveMint with over 3.

title: SpaceX reveals how Starlink Mobile plans to take on AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile
title_bn: SpaceX reveals how Starlink Mobile plans to take on AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile
author: TechPulse
excerpt: SpaceX wants to replace your mobile carrier using rooftop Starlink dishes.
paragraph1: Tushar Mehta / Android AuthorityTL;DR SpaceX confirmed it will build a terrestrial mobile network alongside Starlink satellites. The company says Starlink Mobile will launch by the end of next year with next-gen satellites. SpaceX believes its hybrid network can outperform traditional carriers by eliminating dead zones. When reports emerged that SpaceX was exploring a Starlink-branded mobile carrier, it sounded like an ambitious long-term goal. At the time, the company had reportedly been pitching investors on a consumer wireless service, backed by its $17 billion acquisition of EchoStar’s 65MHz of spectrum and a possible terrestrial network to complement Starlink’s satellites.
paragraph2: Just weeks later, SpaceX has gone from hinting at those plans to openly confirming them.Speaking during the company’s first earnings call since its IPO, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell confirmed (via Fierce Network) that the company intends to build a terrestrial mobile network alongside its satellite infrastructure, laying out the clearest roadmap yet for what Starlink Mobile will eventually become.“The spectrum that we purchased from EchoStar does have terrestrial components, so we definitely intend to build out the terrestrial component,” Shotwell said. Rather than relying solely on satellites, SpaceX wants a hybrid network that combines space- and ground-based infrastructure into what it describes as a “true mobile service.”That hybrid approach is key.
paragraph3: Today, Starlink’s direct-to-cell service operates using around 5MHz of spectrum leased from carrier partners, primarily for basic connectivity outside cellular coverage. Once the EchoStar acquisition closes, SpaceX will have access to 65MHz of spectrum, alongside next-generation satellites that Shotwell said will make Starlink Mobile 100 times better than the current service.A different approach to building a mobile network The company also shared more about how it plans to build its terrestrial network without matching the enormous infrastructure spending of traditional carriers.Instead of deploying large cellular towers everywhere, Elon Musk said SpaceX is developing a distributed network of smaller base stations that could be integrated with existing Starlink installations on homes and businesses.In other words, many of the same rooftops already hosting Starlink dishes today could eventually help deliver mobile coverage as well.
paragraph4: Notably, SpaceX still owns far less spectrum than AT&T, Verizon, or T-Mobile. Rather than trying to beat those carriers at their own game, it wants satellites to fill coverage gaps while smaller terrestrial nodes provide additional capacity where it’s needed.SpaceX expects to win customers away from the three major US carriers by eliminating dead zones and providing more resilient connectivity during natural disasters. Musk went even further, saying the company believes Starlink Mobile could ultimately deliver higher bandwidth than today’s traditional cellular networks.FollowThank you for being part of our community.

title: Google is killing one of Gmail’s most useful power-user features
title_bn: Google is killing one of Gmail’s most useful power-user features
author: TechPulse
excerpt: In January 2027, Gmail will officially discontinue third-party "Send as" address support.
paragraph1: Stephen Headrick / Android AuthorityTL;DR Starting January 2027, Gmail will no longer support sending emails from third-party addresses (such as Yahoo, Outlook, or custom personal domains) via web or mobile apps. The change also eliminates Gmailify and web-based POP mail fetching. However, native Gmail mobile app multi-account support, Gmail-to-Gmail aliases, and Google Workspace “Send as” options will remain unaffected. Affected users must transition to desktop clients (e.g., Thunderbird, Outlook), dedicated email providers, or paid Workspace plans before 2027.
paragraph2: As Google continues refining its web client with features like BCC recipient warnings and custom ‘Help me write’ AI edits, it is also trimming down legacy capabilities. Starting in January 2027, Gmail will officially discontinue support for the “Send as” feature for third-party email addresses, meaning you will no longer be able to send emails from external services like Yahoo, Outlook, or custom domains through your primary Gmail web interface.Google has updated its official Gmail Help documentation to outline the timeline: Important: Starting January 2027, Gmail will no longer support the “Send as” feature for third-party email addresses, such as @yahoo.com or @outlook.com. This change does not affect Google Workspace aliases or other Gmail addresses you own.
paragraph3: According to a dedicated support page detailing third-party email account support in Gmail, Google has to occasionally make a difficult choice to discontinue features that require disproportionate maintenance resources: In our ongoing commitment to ensuring Gmail remains secure, smart, and easy-to-use, we occasionally have the difficult choice to discontinue features that require disproportionate maintenance resources. To that end, we are making changes to how Gmail handles third-party email accounts. The “Send as” feature allows you to send emails from a different address you own, such as a work alias or a non-Gmail account like @hotmail.com, @yahoo.com, and others. However, starting January 2027, you will no longer be able to send mail from third-party email accounts in Gmail on the web or in the Gmail mobile apps on Android and iOS.
paragraph4: You will also no longer be able to add or sync third-party email accounts in Gmail on the web. However, Google is retaining this functionality in the Gmail mobile app, so you can at least check emails from your third-party accounts, even if you can’t send anything as an alias.The deprecation also covers Gmailify, which lets you apply Gmail features like spam protection and inbox organization to your third-party email account, as well as web-based POP mail fetching.Note that Gmail-to-Gmail aliases and Google Workspace “Send as” functionality are not affected by these changes.The announcement sparked quite a discussion on Reddit. Power users who relied on Gmail as a central, unified inbox for personal domains criticized the move as an attempt to push consumers toward paid Google Workspace subscriptions or paid Google One custom-domain tiers, similar to Apple’s iCloud Plus offering.
paragraph5: Users managing family domain routing noted that while inbound email forwarding will still land in their inboxes, responding without revealing their personal @gmail.com address will soon be impossible.Since the deprecation is scheduled for January 2027, affected users have some time to evaluate alternatives. While native mobile mail clients and desktop apps like Thunderbird (which I personally use) or Outlook will continue to support multi-account setups via standard IMAP/POP protocols, those committed to a single web client may need to migrate to dedicated email services or upgrade to a paid Google Workspace account.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: The AI dictation app everyone is talking about just got a powerful new Notetaker
title_bn: The AI dictation app everyone is talking about just got a powerful new Notetaker
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Wispr Flow's new AI Notetaker might make you ditch your Pixel's Recorder app.
paragraph1: Karandeep Singh / Android AuthorityTL;DR Wispr Flow has launched a new AI-powered Notetaker that automatically records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings. The tool can identify speakers by name, search across meetings and messages, and let you ask questions about missed conversations. It also integrates with AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude and supports one-click imports from Granola. Wispr Flow, the AI-powered dictation app that has become popular for turning speech into text across apps, is expanding beyond writing.The company has now launched “Notetaker,” a new AI meeting assistant designed to automatically capture conversations, identify speakers, and generate organized summaries with action items.
paragraph2: The launch pits Wispr Flow against a growing list of AI meeting assistants, but the company is emphasizing accuracy and context rather than just transcription.Wispr FlowWispr Flow claims that Notetaker can capture conversations “exactly as they were said” while identifying participants by name rather than generic labels like Speaker 1 or Speaker 2. If someone is mislabeled, users can also correct it with a single click.Unlike many meeting transcription tools, Notetaker can connect your meeting history with other information you’ve shared with Wispr. Users can search across previous meetings, messages, and emails to find answers, with links back to the original source for context.
paragraph3: Another standout feature is a “What did I miss?” button. If you lose track of a meeting, the AI can summarize the last few minutes of discussion and help you catch up quickly.Wispr FlowOnce a meeting ends, Notetaker automatically generates a structured summary that highlights key decisions, timelines, and next steps, organizing everything by topic instead of dumping a chronological transcript.Wispr is also positioning Notetaker as a research tool before meetings begin.
paragraph4: It can review previous conversations and research external participants (which sounds a bit creepy, to be honest) in the name of giving users relevant context before joining a call.As for availability, Notetaker will work across platforms like Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Slack Huddles, and even informal conversations, as long as audio is available. It can also integrate with AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (MCP), including ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor, allowing users to reference meeting data in their existing AI conversations.For users switching from Granola, Wispr is offering a one-click migration so they can import their existing meeting history without starting from scratch.The only catch is that Notetaker is not available on mobile right now.
paragraph5: Unlike Wispr Flow’s dictation app on Android, Notetaker is only available on Mac for the moment.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Meta And WhatsApp’s Moderation Machines Have A Transparency Problem
title_bn: Meta And WhatsApp’s Moderation Machines Have A Transparency Problem
author: TechPulse
excerpt: WhatsApp today is more than just a messaging app. For millions of users, it serves as the primary channel for…
paragraph1: WhatsApp today is more than just a messaging app. For millions of users, it serves as the primary channel for personal conversations, workplace coordination, and business communication. So when access to WhatsApp accounts disappears overnight, the disruption extends far beyond just chats and messaging. This week, several users across India and other regions reported that their WhatsApp accounts were suddenly placed under review, with the platform saying it was checking “account activity and device information” to ensure compliance with its ‘Terms of Service’. WhatsApp said the review process could take up to 24 hours. While some users regained access within a few hours, others remained locked out or claimed their accounts had been permanently banned without a clear explanation. The incident has raised fresh questions over WhatsApp’s automated enforcement systems, transparency around moderation decisions, and the effectiveness of its grievance redressal process. Sudden WhatsApp Bans, Little Clarity Among those affected was Deepak K Viswanathan, cofounder of Vanaalaya, who took to X after discovering that his WhatsApp account had been banned. “WhatsApp has banned my account. For absolutely no reason. Has anyone else experienced this?
paragraph2: Any idea what the next steps are?” he wrote. His account was restored nearly three hours later after he reached out to Meta support. Speaking to Inc42, Viswanathan said he was left puzzled because he had not engaged in any activity that violated WhatsApp’s policies. “Most of my communications happen through WhatsApp. When something like this happens suddenly, it is unsettling because a major communication channel goes offline when most of your contacts are on the platform,” he said. For political strategist and digital campaign consultant Vikrant Adams, the experience proved far more disruptive. Adams said the WhatsApp account linked to a phone number he has used since 2006-07 was permanently banned without any explanation. According to him, the account was initially marked as “under review”, but the review process was completed automatically before he had an opportunity to challenge the decision. “I got a notification that my account was under review. I didn’t know how the ban happened and the review was automatically done.
paragraph3: Now, I am not able to ask them for review again,” he said. Repeated attempts to contact WhatsApp support only resulted in automated responses, Adams claimed. “If there is no review button, that means it is permanently banned and you can’t use WhatsApp.” He added that creating a fresh account was hardly a viable alternative because his existing number was tied to years of personal and professional relationships. InVideo founder and CEO Sanket Shah also shared on X that his WhatsApp account was placed under review, tagging the messaging platform’s head Kunal Shah. The differing experiences of users whose accounts were restored and those who remain locked out have fuelled calls for greater transparency around why accounts are restricted, how review decisions are made, and what options users have when they believe an error has occurred. The Missing Accountability As complaints mounted across social media, WhatsApp acknowledged that mistakes can occur while enforcing its policies. “We are always working to stay ahead of those trying to abuse our service and ban accounts to help keep other users safe. Sometimes we get this wrong and if we do, we try to fix it as quickly as possible to get people back to chatting,” a WhatsApp spokesperson said. However, the company has not disclosed what triggered the reviews, how many accounts were affected, and whether the restrictions stemmed from a technical issue or an overly aggressive automated enforcement system. paragraph4: For legal and cybersecurity experts, the concern is not that enforcement mistakes happen, but that users receive little information when they do. Mishi Choudhary, founder of the Software Freedom Law Center, India, said WhatsApp is yet to explain what triggered the reviews, how many users were affected, and whether the incident resulted from a technical failure or an overbroad automated system. “It would be irresponsible to speculate without that information,” she said, adding that the episode nevertheless exposed gaps in WhatsApp’s review process, where users can lose access to an essential communication service without understanding what prompted the action. While automated systems remain necessary to tackle spam, scams, and abuse at scale, she said Meta must provide greater accountability by disclosing the number of affected users, the proportion of bans that were reversed, and the safeguards being introduced to prevent similar incidents. She added that while platforms cannot be expected to disclose technical details that could help malicious actors evade detection, simply citing the ‘Terms of Service’ is no longer an adequate explanation, particularly when platforms such as WhatsApp have become critical communication infrastructure. Cybersecurity expert Ritesh Bhatia, founder of V4WEB Cybersecurity, said users should receive clearer explanations whenever enforcement action is taken against their accounts. “Give me a reason so that I can come and fight for it. If not, at least I can come to know what my mistake is,” he said, adding that generic notifications leave users with little opportunity to understand the alleged violation or effectively challenge the platform’s decision. title: ANBERNIC’s new Game Boy Advance SP clone is here for under $60
title_bn: ANBERNIC’s new Game Boy Advance SP clone is here for under $60
author: TechPulse
excerpt: ANBERNIC's new Game Boy Advance SP clone is available for pre-order today. Here's what it will cost you.
paragraph1: TL;DR ANBERNIC’s latest Game Boy Advance SP clone is available for preorder today. The ANBERNIC RG SP has a recommended price of $64.99 and a promo price of $57.99. The new handheld has almost identical specs to the firm’s previous GBA SP copycats.
paragraph2: ANBERNIC previously copied the Game Boy Advance SP design with handhelds like the RG34XXSP and RG35XXSP. Now, the company is returning to the well once again with a new device, which goes on preorder today.The ANBERNIC RG SP is another unabashed Game Boy Advance SP clone, featuring a familiar clamshell design, a near-identical face button layout, and the same 3:2 screen aspect ratio.Pop the hood, and you’ll find specs in line with the firm’s previous Game Boy Advance SP clones. That means a Linux-based OS, a lightweight AllWinner H700 chipset (quad-core Cortex-A53, Mali-G31 MP2 GPU), 1GB of RAM, and 16GB of storage via a microSD card.
paragraph3: Other notable specs include a 3.4-inch IPS panel (720 x 480), a 3,300mAh battery, two microSD card slots, Bluetooth 4.2, Wi-Fi 5, a 3.5mm port, and a lanyard slot.The ANBERNIC RG SP is available for preorder from today (August 5) and has a recommended starting price of $64.
paragraph4: 99 for the model with a single 16GB microSD card. But the company is currently offering a $7 discount, which takes the starting price to $57.99.Either way, this might be worth a look if you want a full-blown Game Boy Advance SP clone. However, the RG34XXSP and RG35XXSP have almost identical specs, while the former model also has dual analog sticks.
paragraph5: So the older device might be the better purchase if you want to play PS1, N64, or PSP games.FollowThank you for being part of our community. Read our Comment Policy before posting.

title: Ted Lasso returns at an important time for Apple TV
title_bn: Ted Lasso returns at an important time for Apple TV
author: TechPulse
excerpt: 2026 is shaping up to be an excellent year for Apple TV. Apple's streaming service has built out an impressive slate that spans returning favorites like Silo and Sugar to all-new hits including OnlyFans-inspired dramedies, terrifying comedies, and pa
paragraph1: 2026 is shaping up to be an excellent year for Apple TV. Apple’s streaming service has built out an impressive slate that spans returning favorites like Silo and Sugar to all-new hits including OnlyFans-inspired dramedies, terrifying comedies, and paranoid tech thrillers. But the most important release might be a feel-good sports sitcom. After what seemed like a definitive finale, Ted Lasso is back with a fourth season that doubles as a soft reboot for the show, mixing up familiar characters with a substantially new cast. And as Apple TV continues its push for a bigger piece of the streaming market, the return of its most culturally impactful series could go a long way toward solidifying its place against more established competitors.The end of season 3, which happened in 2023, promised a lot of change and what seemed like a happy ending for much of the main cast.
paragraph2: Among many other things, Ted (Jason Sudeikis) was heading back to the US to spend time with his son, Roy (Brett Goldstein) had just been promoted to head coach of AFC Richmond, Coach Beard (Brendan Hunt) got married at Stonehenge, and Richmond’s leadership group of Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), Keeley (Juno Temple), and Higgins (Jeremy Swift) were flirting with the idea of launching a women’s team. It had the energy of a sitcom ending, and the episode was even called “So Long, Farewell.” But it’s that fledgling women’s team that spurs the show’s return.The season 4 premiere almost feels like a different show at first, and that largely comes down to location. At the outset, Ted is working part-time at a grocery store in order to have more time to parent, and Rebecca, Keeley, and Higgins have come to Kansas City in an attempt to convince him to be the inaugural coach of the new team. It’s like a reunion episode of sorts, with old friends catching up for the first time in years, which helps viewers understand what has happened in that time.
paragraph3: It also drags out Ted’s inevitable decision to say “yes” across a full episode.Image: AppleThe premiere serves as a transitory moment for this new era of Ted Lasso, and from there the show shifts back to England and takes on a much more familiar feel — but with some significant changes. Part of what makes season 4 feel like a reboot is the players. Ted and most of the rest of the coaching staff and club leadership are back, but the actual team itself is all new. That means that favorites like Jamie Tartt (Phil Dunster), Sam Obisanya (Toheeb Jimoh), and Dani Rojas (Cristo Fernández) aren’t in the show at all aside from some brief mentions (or at least they weren’t featured in any of the five episodes Apple provided press ahead of time). In their place is a scrappy squad of up-and-coming players, and an assistant coach named Alice (Tanya Reynolds) who provides a more stern counterpoint to Ted’s relentless optimism.
paragraph4: It’s a risky bet eschewing beloved characters for a bunch of newcomers, but, at least early on, season 4 of Ted Lasso manages to recapture much of what made the show such a success, but in a new context. The players on Richmond’s women’s side aren’t coddled millionaires, but rather athletes trying to find their way in a still underfunded and undersupported field. One thing I appreciate is that it doesn’t gloss over the very real challenges of women’s football, from lackluster media support and facilities to the rash of devastating injuries that plague its players. This provides plenty of opportunities for Ted to learn and impart his folksy wisdom, and for the eclectic new cast to reflect this challenging landscape. There’s an intense goalkeeper who was ignored by bigger clubs because she refuses to wear gloves (Jude Mack), a mom who made the team after spontaneously deciding to attend an open tryout (Faye Marsay), and a star striker who is balancing her athletic career with getting a law degree (Abbie Hern).Recapturing the exact magic that made Ted Lasso’s early seasons such a phenomenon is probably impossible, and the new season is premiering at a very different time for Apple TV.
paragraph5: Much has happened since its 2020 debut — service-defining shows like Severance and Pluribus didn’t even exist then — but many of those changes also bode well for Ted Lasso. Not only is Apple TV seemingly on an upward trajectory, but a controversial yet very successful men’s World Cup has reignited interest in the sport (particularly in the US), while the next women’s World Cup looms on the horizon. Those seem like prime circumstances for an impactful return for Ted and friends. The show may have changed, but its importance for Apple hasn’t.Ted Lasso season 4 starts streaming on Apple TV on August 5th.Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

title: InRisk Labs Raises $27 Mn To Scale AI-Led Reinsurance Platform EarthRe
title_bn: InRisk Labs Raises $27 Mn To Scale AI-Led Reinsurance Platform EarthRe
author: TechPulse
excerpt: GIFT City-based insurtech startup InRisk Labs has raised $27 Mn (about ₹256 Cr) in a Series A funding round co-led…
paragraph1: SUMMARYInRisk Labs has raised $27 Mn in a Series A funding round, while its subsidiary EarthRe has secured an IFSCA reinsurance licence The funding and licence position InRisk Labs to scale AI-led reinsurance offerings as demand for climate-risk and catastrophe coverage grows in India InRisk Labs develops technology for parametric insurance and reinsurance, while EarthRe offers non-life reinsurance across climate risk, property, crop, marine, motor and other specialty segments GIFT City-based insurtech startup InRisk Labs has raised $27 Mn (about ₹256 Cr) in a Series A funding round co-led by Bessemer Venture Partners and Northpoint Capital. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the startup’s underwriting, actuarial, catastrophe modelling and AI capabilities. It also plans to expand into new non-life insurance segments, develop parametric and structured reinsurance products, and meet regulatory capital requirements to scale its subsidiary EarthRe’s operations in India’s $10 Bn reinsurance market.
paragraph2: Alongside the fundraise, the startup said EarthRe Insurance IFSC has secured a reinsurance licence from the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA). With this, EarthRe has become the first incorporated reinsurer to receive a licence from the IFSC at GIFT City, InRisk Labs said. Founded in 2024 by Aavrit Singhal, Siddesh Ramasubramanian, Shivakhumar R S, and Malay Kumar Poddar, InRisk Labs builds technology for parametric insurance, which pays out automatically when predefined events such as extreme weather occur, and for reinsurance, which helps insurers manage large risks.
paragraph3: Under the group’s structure, InRisk Labs will continue building the technology, data and risk intelligence stack, while EarthRe will operate as the regulated reinsurance business serving India and other Global South markets. EarthRe focuses on non-life reinsurance, offering coverage across natural catastrophe (NatCat), climate risk, property, crop, marine cargo, motor, and other specialty segments. It uses catastrophe modelling, climate-risk analytics, and AI-powered underwriting to develop structured reinsurance solutions.
paragraph4: InRisk Labs competes with the likes of EigenRisk, IBISA and Mitti Labs in the climate risk, parametric insurance and reinsurance space. The development comes amid rising exposure to natural catastrophe risks and a widening insurance protection gap in India, underscoring the need for advanced climate-risk assessment tools and technology-led insurance solutions. The investment also marks Bessemer Venture Partners’ latest bet on the insurtech space.
paragraph5: Earlier this year, the VC firm led the $15 Mn Series B funding round of cyber risk and insurance startup Mitigata. According to Swiss Re’s report, India’s insurance market is expected to grow at a real annual rate of 6.9% between 2026 and 2030, making it the fastest-growing major insurance market globally.

title: WhatsApp just solved some of the most annoying group chat problems
title_bn: WhatsApp just solved some of the most annoying group chat problems
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Finally, your family group might stop being complete mayhem.
paragraph1: Edgar Cervantes / Android AuthorityTL;DR WhatsApp is making group chats smarter with poll deadlines, anonymous voting, and the ability to edit poll questions for 15 minutes @all mentions now reach everyone, including members who’ve muted the chat, though users can disable these notifications in Settings. Creating spin-off group chats is now easier, letting you start a new group from an existing one with a single tap. If you’ve ever tried organizing something in a busy WhatsApp group, you’ll probably recognize the chaos. Someone votes after the deadline, another person changes the topic halfway through, and before you know it, you’re scrolling through dozens of messages just to figure out what everyone agreed on. Thankfully, Meta is now rolling out a handful of updates that aim to make group chats feel a lot less messy.One of the biggest improvements is for polls.
paragraph2: You’ll now be able to set a closing time, so voting automatically ends when the deadline arrives. That’s especially useful if you’re deciding where to eat, picking a movie for movie night, or collecting responses before booking tickets. Once the poll closes, late votes won’t keep changing the outcome.Privacy is also getting a small but welcome upgrade. Instead of showing who voted for what, WhatsApp now lets you hide voters’ names. That could make people more comfortable sharing honest opinions, whether it’s choosing a team activity, voting on office plans, or settling a friendly debate without feeling pressured by everyone else’s choices.
paragraph3: And if you accidentally publish a poll with a typo or a confusing option, you won’t have to delete it and start over. WhatsApp will let you edit the poll question for up to 15 minutes after it has been posted, giving you enough time to fix mistakes before the conversation moves on.Meta is also refining how @all mentions work. Tagging @all will notify every member of the group, even if they’ve muted notifications for that chat. That’s useful when there’s genuinely important information everyone needs to see, like a venue change, a last-minute cancelation, or an urgent announcement.
